liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (3 reviews, 1 other source): Reviewer singles out the Dark Star into The Other One sequence as the show's highlight; The roughly hour-long Dark Star into The Other One is called the finest example of the band's symphonic improvisation [4][11][12][14]

## Setlist highlights

- **Little Sadie**: rare: 7 archived performances [23]
- **Wake Up Little Susie**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 9 archived performances [23]
- **Katie Mae**: rare: 10 archived performances [23]

## The recordings

- **gd1970-02-13.sbd.miller.97613.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 24 songs; 228 min; rated 5/5 by 12 [1]
- **gd1970-02-13.sbd.miller.fix-97613.97639.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 24 songs; 228 min; rated 4.64/5 by 22 [2]
- **gd1970-02-13.176321.sbd.miller.flac1644**: soundboard; 24 songs; 229 min [3]
- **gd1970-02-13.123814.aud.cooper.flac16**: audience recording; 22 songs; 166 min; rated 4.75/5 by 4 [4]

## Around the show

- Show displays country, folk, blues and motown influences; the jams reference each other and familiar tunes such as a Simon & Garfunkel song [12]
- David Gans played about 90 minutes of unreleased material from the 2/13 and 2/14/70 shows on KPFA; the 2/14 Dark Star was among them [18]
- The acoustic set and the early show of 2/13/70 were reportedly never officially released [20]
- Late show was one continuous set, played in electric, acoustic, then electric segments; Allman Brothers Band also on the bill [3]
- Late show was one continuous set, played in electric, acoustic, then electric segments; Allman Brothers Band also on the bill [4]
- Reviewer ranks this Dark Star/Other One just above Live Dead as an example of the band's improvisation [12]
- Having both Dark Star and The Other One in a single show is rare after 1970 [14]
- Dick's Picks 4 is described as a badly butchered, incomplete document of this performance [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1970-02-13.sbd.miller.97613.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel (7 inch 1/2 Track at 15ips) -> Dat (48k) [1]. Also: Source is soundboard from DATs lent by Rob Eaton; late-show disc changes are seamless; Between-song tunings in the late show and Uncle John's Band are patched from shnid 18114; Uncle John's Band is cut [1]
- **gd1970-02-13.sbd.miller.fix-97613.97639.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel (7 inch 1/2 Track at 15ips) -> Dat (48k) [2]. Also: Fixed version of the Miller soundboard transfer repairs digital noise in Little Sadie; from Rob Eaton's DATs; Late-show tunings and a cut Uncle John's Band are patched from shnid 18114 [2]
- **gd1970-02-13.176321.sbd.miller.flac1644**: transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  February 13, 2026; source: SBD > Master Reel (7 inch 1/2 Track at 15ips) > DAT (48k) [3]. Also: Soundboard transfer from tapes provided by Rob Eaton, with late-show tunings patched from another source [3]
- **gd1970-02-13.123814.aud.cooper.flac16**: taped by Jim Cooper; source: Late show. Recorded by Jim Cooper from seat # BB 108 (2nd row Center) Hitachi trq-222, 2 Hitachi mikes; Transferred > sony d5pro2 > dbx 2231 EQ > sony rcd w500c [4]
